name: decompose
why: Reverse-engineers running docker environments into compose files, a useful way to see how a stack was assembled.

brief.what_it_is: decompose is a command-line tool that reverse-engineers a running Docker environment. It takes the network connections of your containers and exports them as a graph or structured file: graphviz dot, structurizr DSL, compose YAML, PlantUML, a pseudographical tree, a JSON stream, statistics (node, connection and listen-port counts), or CSV with columns name, listen and outbounds. Its input is the live Docker daemon (via DOCKER_HOST and related variables), and its output goes to stdout by default. It can also load saved JSON streams and merge them.
brief.why_it_exists: The author needed to visualize and inspect a large dockerized legacy system (more than 470 containers) with no schemes and very little documentation. The README says the closest existing tools did not fit: some only produce compose YAML, and others take links and ports from compose configuration, which can miss connections.
brief.how_it_works: It collects connections from the containers rather than reading compose files. On Linux as root it uses nsenter, which works even for scratch-based containers. As non-root or on other OSes it runs netstat inside each container, and containers without netstat yield no connections. Unix-socket matching on Linux needs root and uses inode matching. Output formats are sorted, so they can be committed to version control and diffed.

commands_seen.context: Saves the full JSON stream of the running environment to a file, run as root so the nsenter strategy is used.
Writes the connection graph in graphviz dot format to a file (default output is JSON).
Restricts the scan to tcp and udp connections and writes dot output.
Merges several saved JSON streams, skips external hosts, filters to tcp, and writes dot output.
Loads a saved stream, enriches it with a metadata file, and writes a structurizr DSL workspace.
Runs automatic clusterization with similarity 0.6 and writes structurizr DSL.
Pipes the dot output through graphviz to render an SVG of the running stack, as in the README's example.
Starts the redis-cluster example stack that the README uses to reproduce the sample graph.
Workaround the README gives so that gephi can load edges from the generated graphviz file.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew, the README points to prebuilt binaries, deb and rpm packages from the GitHub releases page (Linux, FreeBSD, macOS, Windows) and a Docker image on Docker Hub. Full scanning as root on Linux needs sudo, since the nsenter path requires it. Connection settings come from environment variables: DOCKER_HOST (connection URI), DOCKER_CERT_PATH (directory with key.pem, cert.pm and ca.pem; the README spells cert.pem as cert.pm), DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY (enable TLS verification), and IN_DOCKER_PROC_ROOT (host-mounted /proc root for running inside a container). The README does not describe a first-run setup beyond this.
brief.standout: The deep mode (-deep) introspects connections between processes inside containers, not just between containers. Automatic clusterization (-cluster auto:<similarity>) groups services by port-set similarity, and clusters can also be defined with expr-language rules. Sorted output makes the results diffable in version control.
brief.status: unknown. The README has CI, coverage (98.0%), Go Report Card, release and FOSSA badges, and it is listed in awesome-go. The fetched text carries no release date, last commit date or maintenance note, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: Only established and listen connections are listed, so short-lived connections are missed; the README suggests a snapshots.sh script for that. Non-root or non-Linux runs need netstat inside containers, and containers without it show no connections. Unix-socket collection works only as root on Linux. The compose YAML output is for system overview only: it can lack information even in -full mode or contain cycles between nodes. Gephi needs a sed fix to load the dot output. The README mentions no Windows-specific notes. The badge shows an MIT license.
quotes: I was in need for a tool to visualize and inspect big (more than 470 containers) dockerized legacy system without any schemes and having a bare minimum of documentation
all output formats are sorted, thus can be placed to any `vcs` to observe changes
